title: Six-class secp256k1 rho at 125.858232: walk groups of 256 on the shared-row pass-2 / one-address-rule package

claims.statement: For a uniform full-production secp256k1 input Q=[x]P, the classical cold six-class negation-plus-GLV parallel Pollard-rho attack of proof.md and upstream-proof.md halts on every run with total work at most 2^125.858232 target-group-operation equivalents under classical-group-work-v2 (C=1000). It builds on bradcush's 886e6f54 / a00774d8 line (one address rule for both y parities and shorter plain fused pass 1), keeping the walk, census, kappa, pass 2 and meter, with walk groups of 256 (LSR #8) and exact plain round fixed overhead accounting: pass1p is 125.5078125 instructions per walk, pass2 432.5078125, plain round fixed work 24,793 + 1271.015625 = 26,064.015625 -> share 26065/2^20, and the plain step price is 558.015625 + 26065/2^20 = 558.040483. pass1f is 129.015625, and compare rounds charge extra arithmetic 3.5078125 plus compare fixed delta (384/2^20) per walk (a hard row). The declared run executes both fused copies (0 mismatches against the address rule, odd borrows injected), arrive.s, the loops and all 3,090 exit stubs. kappa = 1.0001 follows from the shipped hazard census. Declared dependencies (proof.md section 6): 886e6f54 (immediate), a00774d8, c06f6691, 4ac17b66, 445f9a1c, cbea87bf, 4c8222cc, 673640ef, 0a1c5772, 610c8e49, 6a6cb91c, 5f1ae3ce, 4595bad7, 01488655, 2bd168b5, daf2c741, a9297fb0, 807e4bf5, b5de673a, 02feb284 (20 total; 4b4defe7 credited in base proof only). Recovery probability is greater than 0.39000019 and therefore at least 0.39 (failure rows 1.0103e-7 < 1.1e-7). Peak memory < 2^72 bytes; preprocessing capped at 2^59 units and included; no advice. Exact ledger: S_ops = 1.0001*S0 = 2^126.6995433, phase 1 = 2^125.857985, hard extras = 2^111.795750, random extras = 2^98.827042, allowance = 2^112.736242, W_ledger = 2^125.858231149 <= 1000*2^125.858232 milli-units; Markov ratio 0.0000646602 < 0.000065; certificate.py checks the claim and that 125.858231 fails, in exact arithmetic. No prior acceptance, review verdict or official score is a premise. This is an analytic heuristic bound, not a practical break.

experiments.purpose: Part A: production secp256k1 checks of the walk identities and the canonical-index rule; Part B: a scaled toy pipeline of the checkpoint-only walk (even-y key, per-trail phases, compares every 128th round) on subgroups of y^2=x^3+7 with node routing, a check that the old and the production compare rule reach the same endpoints, and a long-trail trap test; kernels: Python limb ports of the field kernels against big integers, and the shipped loops (with rare exits on constructed inputs entering every stub), both copies of the fused pass 1, emitter wrappers and arrival rows executed by an AArch64 interpreter (kernels/a64.py) against affine secp256k1, a bit-exact model and the exact canonical rule, with instruction counts and the ledger recomputed. The toy run does not meter production instructions or implement 2^20 concurrent walks.
